findings: Species identity is correct: the adult specimen has white plumage, a long strongly downcurved red-orange bill, reddish-pink bare facial skin, pale blue eye, long reddish-pink legs, and black outer primaries—the diagnostic White Ibis combination shown by the references and live sources.
The scientific name Eudocimus albus and family Threskiornithidae are correct.

The primary specimen is complete and singular, with one head, one closed bill, two wings, two legs with plausible unwebbed wading feet, and one short tail. The detached spread-wing and head studies are clearly supplementary and anatomically consistent with the primary specimen.
Both depicted heads have consistent, closed, tapered bills with the appropriate direction and degree of decurvature; neither mandible appears truncated, reversed, or inconsistently projected.
The detached wing correctly shows white coverts and black outer flight feathers. The standing specimen appropriately shows a limited black primary projection near the folded wingtip.
Every visible prose line accurately reproduces the proposed habitat, behavior, measurements, and field marks without spelling, number, duplication, omission, substitution, or word-order errors.

The displayed 53–70 cm length, 593–1,261 g weight, and 90–105 cm wingspan are supported by the cited Wikipedia description, though Cornell and Audubon publish narrower guide ranges derived from different measurement summaries.

The ruler is internally consistent: 53 cm (21 in) is at the bottom, 70 cm (28 in) is at the top, values increase upward, four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks divide the range into five proportional segments, and the repeated body-length range agrees with both endpoints.
“SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” clearly prevents the ruler from implying that the printed specimen is life-size.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
